title: Plugin Redesign
meta: A cleaner, modern interface for your WooCommerce plugin settings and screens, keeping your users and data. From $150, delivered in 7 days or less.
h1: WooCommerce plugin redesign, easier for store owners
overview: Store owners judge a plugin by its settings page. We review your admin screens and redesign them so options are grouped, labels are plain and previews show what each setting does. We build the new interface to match the WordPress and WooCommerce admin, using React components where they help, and keep your saved settings and data untouched. We also check it on mobile admin and common color schemes.

pkgs.blurb: A tidier look for up to three admin screens.
Redesigned main screens with tabs, search and inline help.
A complete refresh with a setup wizard and a dashboard widget.

faq: Will my customers' saved settings be kept?
Yes. We change how options are shown, not how they are stored. Existing settings load into the new screens exactly as saved, and we test the update on a copy with real data.
Do you change the store front end too?
Only if your plugin has public output, and only if you ask. This service focuses on the admin screens. We can quote storefront work next to it if your plugin has widgets or blocks.
Do you use React for the new screens?
Where it helps, yes. WordPress ships React components, so we use them for dynamic screens and plain PHP templates for simple ones. We avoid heavy extra libraries to keep the plugin light.
Can you match my own branding?
Yes. We keep the interface native to WordPress and add your logo, accent color and wording. A fully custom look is possible but can make the screens feel foreign to store owners.
desc:
A WooCommerce plugin admin redesign gives your settings and screens a cleaner, clearer interface that store owners can understand at a glance. Ecom Swift LLC reorganizes the layout, rewrites labels and builds the new screens while keeping your saved settings and data.

## What is a WooCommerce plugin admin redesign?

It is a rework of the screens a store owner uses inside the WordPress admin: the settings page, list tables, setup steps and any dashboard area your plugin adds. The goal is a better layout and clearer language, not a change in what the plugin does.

The new interface follows the look of WordPress and WooCommerce, so it feels familiar. React components are used where they help, such as live previews or tabs that switch without reloading the page.

## Why does a plugin's settings page matter so much?

The settings page is the plugin's real product face. Store owners rarely read documentation. They open the page, look for the option they need and decide in a minute whether the plugin is easy or painful.

A long single page with unlabeled checkboxes, technical terms and no explanations creates doubt. Owners fear that a wrong click will break the store, so they leave settings unchanged or deactivate the plugin. Support questions that start with "where do I find..." often point to layout problems, not missing features.

## How a clearer interface helps users and support

When options are grouped by task, owners find them faster and set them correctly. When each setting has a plain label and a short explanation, fewer people need help. When a preview shows what a setting changes, owners try more of your features.

For you, this means fewer tickets about basic configuration and more users who reach the features that make the plugin valuable. A tidy interface also signals that the plugin is actively cared for.

## What a good plugin interface includes

- Settings grouped into clear sections by task, not by code structure.
- Plain-language labels in place of internal names.
- Short help text and tooltips next to complex options.
- Tabs and a search field when the plugin has many settings.
- Previews that show the effect of a setting where possible.
- Consistent spacing, buttons and notices matching the WordPress admin.
- A setup wizard that guides new installs through the essentials.
- A dashboard widget with a few key numbers, in higher packages.
- Checks on a phone-size admin and in different admin color schemes.
- An accessibility pass covering focus order, contrast and labels.

## What we do

We begin with an audit of your current screens. We list every option, note where wording is unclear and group settings by what the owner is trying to do. We then share a layout for review, with before and after screenshots, and in Premium work we provide editable Figma designs.

Once you approve, we build the new screens, move each existing setting into its new place and test that saved values still load and save correctly. We do not touch the store front end unless you ask for it. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of screens, the use of tabs and search, and whether a wizard, widget and accessibility pass are added.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which settings your support team is asked about most.
- Keep option names in the database unchanged.
- Use short, concrete labels such as "Send order email to".
- Share your brand colors if you want them reflected.
- Test the new screens with someone who has never used the plugin.

**Avoid:**
- Hiding important options deep in nested menus.
- Using technical jargon in labels.
- Relying on color alone to show status.
- Removing settings that long-time users still depend on.
- Cramming every option onto one page.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a plugin that has grown over the years and now has a crowded settings page. It suits a founder preparing a public launch who wants the interface to look finished. It also suits a team whose support inbox is full of setup questions that a clearer layout would answer.

## What we need from you

Send the plugin code or a staging site with the plugin installed, a list of the screens in scope and your branding if you have it. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a developer or collaborator user. Your customers' saved settings stay in place, because we change the interface, not the stored data.
